name: radio-group

frames.best_why: All four rows and prices are readable with the chosen row shown and no cursor covering them.

tagline: Stacked pricing rows where one circle marks the chosen plan.
summary: A plan chooser: a card lists four subscription rows, each with a small circle, a name, a short description and a price. Clicking a row moves the single selection and highlights that row.
appearance: A dark rounded card with a bold 'Choose a plan' heading and one muted line, then four stacked rows. Each row holds a small circle, a bold plan name over a dim description, and a price at the right; the chosen row gets a lighter border and fill.
behaviour: Clicking a row fills its circle with a dot and moves the lighter border to it, so only one stays chosen. The change is instant, and keyboard focus draws a ring around the circle.
demo_content: Four plans: Hobby free, Pro at $20 per month, Team at $49 per month and Enterprise priced custom.
search_phrases: choose one plan from a list
pricing options with a single choice
circle markers that select one row
pick one option from stacked cards
single selection list in a form
highlighted row for the chosen option
use_when: Exactly one of a few clearly labelled options must be chosen and easy comparison matters.
avoid_when: Rows show only two short lines, so plans needing feature lists are better built as cards.
customise: You supply the rows and circles as children; value or defaultValue controls the choice, and colours, gap and row styling come from classes.
weight_why: Four small circles and labels with colour transitions only.

a11y.note: Arrow keys move the choice and labels are linked by id, but the chosen row is communicated mostly by colour and a 6px dot.

issues: The chosen row differs only by a faint border and slight fill, easy to miss on a dark page
The 6px dot inside a 16px circle is a weak selection mark
No submit action follows the choice, so the demo shows no result
polish_why: Ordered plan list with clear prices; the chosen row barely stands out on the dark stage.
